title: Wellbeing and resilience
subject: RSE
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
source_note: Date, period and exact outcome supplied verbatim in the owner's Week1 brief, LAUNCH Weekly Spring row148. Accepted LAUNCH Autumn2 structure/style used as reference only, with clean newly authored content, metadata and explicit tiered packs. Source workbook not reopened. Official statutory guidance in force from September2026 and public-health information checked for the narrow lesson content; no claim that one lesson covers all statutory RSHE.

definitions.wellbeing: How a person is doing in everyday life. It includes feeling supported, having things that matter to them, and being able to manage daily life or get help.
definitions.mental_health: A part of everyone's health, linked to thoughts, feelings and coping with daily life. Everyone has mental health. This does not mean everyone has a mental health condition.
definitions.resilience: Adapting to a setback or change, recovering in your own time, and using support when needed. It can include rest, a different plan or asking for help. It never means having to put up with harm.

key_points: Everyone has mental health, just as everyone has physical health.
Wellbeing can change; feeling upset sometimes does not by itself mean a mental health condition.
Resilience includes support and changing a plan. Nobody has to cope alone.
A small step may help wellbeing; it is not a guaranteed fix or a substitute for needed support.

wheel.title: My wellbeing wheel

domains.label: Sleep
domains.meaning: Rest and a routine that supports sleep.
domains.example: Prepare one calm wind-down step at a time that suits the learner.

domains.label: Movement
domains.meaning: Safe, accessible ways to move that suit the person.
domains.prompt: What type of movement could fit?
domains.example: Ask staff about a short, suitable movement break. No exercise is required in this lesson.

domains.label: People
domains.prompt: Who could offer safe support, by role?
domains.example: Arrange a brief check-in with a trusted member of school staff.

domains.label: Purpose
domains.meaning: Something that feels worthwhile, such as an interest, learning or helping.
domains.prompt: What small activity could feel worthwhile?
domains.example: Set aside a few minutes for an interest or a useful task.

domains.label: Downtime
domains.meaning: Time for rest or enjoyment without a performance demand.
domains.prompt: What could make a pause useful?
domains.example: Choose a quiet activity for an agreed break.

wheel.instruction: Use the five sections as prompts. Add a word, symbol or optional mark if you wish. Leave any section blank. There are no scores to add or right-shaped wheels.
wheel.privacy: Your personal wheel stays private and with you. Do not put a name, health history, family details, sleep hours or private worry on it. You do not have to show or explain it to the pair or staff. Use the invented learner instead, leave blank or pass if you prefer.
wheel.not_test: This wheel is an authored reflection aid, not a test, validated scale, diagnosis, target score or measure of how healthy a person is.

scene.title: A new weekly routine
scene.text: A learner starts a new weekly routine. They are unsure what to do first and want some time to unwind. They enjoy making things. A trusted member of school staff can explain the new routine. The learner chooses one short quiet activity during an agreed break and plans to ask the staff member for a check-in.
discussion: What might support this learner's wellbeing?
Where does the learner show resilience?
Which wheel sections could connect? More than one can fit.
scene.model: The learner uses people by planning a safe check-in, and downtime by choosing a quiet activity. An interest could also give purpose. Asking for help and adjusting the plan can show resilience.

action_plan.instruction: Each learner chooses ONE realistic change, privately, for one wheel area. The change may make an existing helpful habit easier to keep, such as agreeing when or where it fits, rather than add another demand. If a personal plan does not feel suitable, plan one step for the invented learner instead. No plan or personal detail has to be shared.
fields: When or where it could fit: ____________________
If a barrier gets in the way: ____________________
A time or chance to review it: ____________________
action_plan.model: For the invented learner: during the next agreed break, try a short quiet making activity. Ask staff what materials are already available. If materials are not available, choose a quiet drawing or reading option. Review whether the step was useful at a later agreed check-in.
realistic_test: Within the learner's choices, access and resources, or names needed support.
Has a simple time or cue and an alternative if a barrier appears.
action_plan.rule: One change PER learner, not five changes or one per wheel section. No required spending, exercise, sleep target, contact with family, unsupported action or promise to feel better. Context and access differ; barriers are not personal failure.

self_assessment.title: Learning self-check
items: I can explain wellbeing, mental health and resilience in plain words.
I can suggest one realistic step and a support or alternative if needed.
I know how to ask for help privately.
self_assessment.note: Tick only what describes the learning today. This is not a mood, symptom or mental-health score. All boxes start blank; pass or use a fictional example.

help_route: Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff for help to find an age-appropriate route. No named service, number, website or online task is given. Seek help if a concern persists, worsens, affects everyday life or feels unsafe; you do not need a diagnosis first. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school's urgent procedure.
step_out: Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.
safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of the lesson pack, book tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school's separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. Private wheels/plans are not collected, photographed, displayed or compared for assessment. Scribing a personal card is only by agreement; the learner keeps it.
practice_rule: All class questions, paired discussion and worked examples use the invented third-person learner. Pair talk is optional and uses the story, never a partner's wheel or health. Invite private personal wheel/one-change reflection, with fictional alternative, blank or pass equally valid. Do not ask about personal mental health, symptoms, sleep, family or current feelings in front of anyone. Record learning through fictional explanations, not private health information.

routes.Supported: Use the same age-respectful five-domain wheel. Offer the word bank, two example choices, a sentence frame and a completed fictional example. Pointing, drawing, usual aid or exact scribe/readback valid. Choose one realistic step with support and record content prompts.
routes.Independent: Use the glossary, wheel prompts, visible model and usual aids. Explain the fictional example, privately choose one realistic change or fictional equivalent, and identify needed support or a barrier. Record actual independent choices and any prompts honestly.
routes.Aspire: Keep all normal aids. Evaluate two plausible steps for the invented learner, explain the more realistic choice, and adapt it for a barrier without blaming the learner. Still choose only one step. Extra personal disclosure, more changes or longer writing are not required.

tiered_packs.rule: Three separate editable/print packs at lesson root. Each covers the same outcome, five domains, one chosen change and learning-only self-check, with different scaffolding. Shared private wheel card is in Support Cards; print once, not all routes.

success: Explain the three key ideas without stigma.

Identify support or an alternative if a barrier appears.
timing: Quiet set-up, preview lesson and discreet pause route. No current-feelings question.
Fictional claim check: everyone has mental health.
Three meanings and worked fictional example; check understanding.
Private claim/hinge with parallel recheck;15–16 reset included.
16–22 private wheel or fictional alternative;22–27 one realistic step using chosen tier;27–28 reset included.
Fictional explanation and learning self-check;33–34 reset included. Private wheel/plan not collected.
One next step and own response in usual mode.
One private learning check and generic help route.

hinge.question: A learner faces a setback. Which response can show resilience?
hinge.A: They must cope alone and hide every feeling.
hinge.B: They can pause, adapt the plan or ask for safe support.
hinge.decision: Check privately by words, pointing or usual aid. If B or a safe equivalent with a reason, proceed. If A, unclear/no response, re-model supported adaptation and use the parallel check. Pass is not a wrong answer.

parallel.question: What can a wellbeing wheel tell us?
parallel.A: It can prompt reflection and one possible next step.
parallel.B: It can diagnose a mental health condition from its shape.

misconceptions: Resilience means never feeling upset or putting up with harm.
Feelings can vary. Resilience can include rest, support, safe boundaries and changing a plan or situation.
A wheel score or one feeling proves a mental health condition, and a small habit guarantees a fix.
Everyone has mental health. This wheel has no diagnostic score. A small step may help, while support can still be needed.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Explicit short definitions, worked example, glossary, visible model, task frames and one chosen step. Flexible grouping for a pair; reduced written load and extra processing time.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Choice, wait time, familiar aid, pointing/drawing, exact scribe and readback. Pair discussion optional; no requirement for speech or eye contact.
adaptations.SEMH: Predictable content, third-person class questions, privacy for wheel/action plan, blank/pass/fictional alternative, pre-agreed discreet step-out and supported return. No comparison or personal questioning.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Usual accessible print/seating/communication access and quiet resets. Movement is a planning option suited to the person, never an imposed activity or physical test.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Explain wellbeing, resilience and purpose with brief examples. Usual language support can convey the learner's own chosen words.

cold_call_label: Optional private fictional check bank; no public personal questions.

cold_call.F: Which word fits asking for support after a change?
cold_call.M: Which two wheel areas connect to the story, and why?
cold_call.H: Which step is realistic if the learner has limited time or materials?

ta_focus.I_do: Reinforce three meanings without labelling ordinary feelings as conditions. Check the fictional example with normal aids.
ta_focus.We_do: Offer story choices and a frame. Keep personal wheel/plan private; support only by agreement and never read it aloud.
ta_focus.Independent: Observe learning through fictional explanations and chosen route tasks; log prompts and usual modes. Do not collect private reflection. Acknowledge pause signal, supervise and route any disclosure to safeguarding lead.

prompt_ladder: Point to the place or instruction.
Model the first step only, then return the task.
evidence: Staff Evidence Sheet records explanation of the three ideas, an appropriate fictional wheel-area link, a realistic fictional step with support/barrier, learning self-check if offered, usual mode/prompts, one NS and own response. No personal wheel ratings, plan details, health/family history, names or disclosures. Private personal change remains the learner's choice; fictional evidence is equally valid. Do not infer health status, improvement or diagnosis from learning performance.
marking: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.
where_this_leads: This helps me plan a manageable next step, adapt to change and ask for support in learning or future work.
scope: Week1 only. Week2 andWeek3 follow one per return after acceptance/full brief. Weeks4–5 held for owner decision and not built. No later lesson content is included.

paragraphs: Teacher and cover planner
Wellbeing and resilience
Thursday 7 January 2027 · P4 · 40 minutes · Year A
LAUNCH · pair aged 14–16 · Spring 1 Week 1 · formative
Theme Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Exact outcome
Wellbeing, resilience & mental health.
Source: owner brief, LAUNCH Weekly Spring row 148. Accepted Autumn 2 structure is a style reference only. The source workbook was not reopened.
Purpose and success

Explain three ideas without stigma, link a practical idea to a wheel area and choose one realistic change with support or fallback. Assess fictional learning only; personal wheel and plan remain private. A blank, pass or fictional alternative is valid.
Non specialist preparation

Read Staff Answers for definitions, case and checks. Print one tier per learner, Support Cards pages 1–2 once, glossary and staff Evidence Sheet. Prepare books/usual aids. Quietly pre-agree the pause signal, supervised route and staff response. Use fictional examples; no personal details are needed.
Where this leads
This helps me plan a manageable next step, adapt to change and ask for support in learning or future work.
Forty minute sequence
All forty minutes include three one-minute resets: 15–16, 27–28 and 33–34. No public current-feeling check. Pair talk is optional.
Teaching and response routes
Arrival and starter

0–4: calm set-up, predict the lesson sequence and remind learners of the discreet supervised pause route. 4–6: use the fictional claim that everyone has mental health. Explain that this does not mean everyone has a mental health condition. No current-feelings question.
Model and guided check

6–11: teach the three definitions with the invented learner. Asking staff for support and adapting a plan can show resilience. Check one story link privately. 11–15: hinge B and parallel A if needed. 15–16: quiet reset. Keep the visible model and usual aids.
Private practice and learning

16–22: invite the private five-area wheel or fictional equivalent, blank or pass. 22–27: each learner chooses ONE realistic change; a change may make an existing helpful habit easier to keep, such as agreeing when or where it fits. 27–28 reset. 28–33: capture fictional explanation and learning self-check only. 33–34 reset. 34–38: one next step and learner response. 38–40: private learning exit and generic help route.
Supported

Use the same age-respectful five-domain wheel. Offer the word bank, two example choices, a sentence frame and a completed fictional example. Pointing, drawing, usual aid or exact scribe/readback valid. Choose one realistic step with support and record content prompts.
Independent

Use the glossary, wheel prompts, visible model and usual aids. Explain the fictional example, privately choose one realistic change or fictional equivalent, and identify needed support or a barrier. Record actual independent choices and any prompts honestly.
Aspire

Keep all normal aids. Evaluate two plausible steps for the invented learner, explain the more realistic choice, and adapt it for a barrier without blaming the learner. Still choose only one step. Extra personal disclosure, more changes or longer writing are not required.
Worked model and fade

For the invented learner: during the next agreed break, try a short quiet making activity. Ask staff what materials are already available. If materials are not available, choose a quiet drawing or reading option. Review whether the step was useful at a later agreed check-in. The quiet activity is the one chosen change; asking staff about materials is support for that step, not a second goal. Show the model first, then leave a choice and reason to the learner. Retain glossary, frames, wheel prompts and normal aids.
TA focus

I do: reinforce meanings without labelling ordinary feelings as a condition. We do: offer fictional choices and a frame. Independent: observe fictional explanations and record prompts, acknowledge pause signal, maintain supervision and route any disclosure through safeguarding. Personal card support is only by agreement.
Aids for each task
Each task keeps a short word bank, sentence starter and visible model. The separate tier packs adapt scaffolding while retaining the same outcome, five areas, one change and learning self-check.
Starter claim
Words: everyone, health, thoughts, feelings
Start: Everyone has mental health because ... .
Model: Mental health is part of everyone's health.
Model check
Words: wellbeing, resilience, support, change
Start: The learner shows resilience by ... .
Model: The learner asks for help and adapts the plan.
Private hinge
Words: pause, adapt, support, safe
Start: A helpful response could be ... because ... .
Model: A helpful response could be asking staff because the learner needs a clearer first step.
Wheel reflection
Words: sleep, movement, people, purpose, downtime
Start: For the invented learner, ... could support ... .
Model: A safe check-in could support the people area.
One realistic change
Words: one step, cue, support, barrier, review
Start: They could try ... at ... . If ... , they could ... .
Model: They could choose a quiet activity at an agreed break. If materials are missing, they could choose another quiet activity.
Learning self-check
Words: explain, example, prompt, help
Start: I can explain ... using the example ... .
Model: I can explain resilience using the learner's supported plan change.
Feedback and exit
Words: next step, response, adult, private
Start: A next step in the story could be ... .
Model: A next step in the story could be checking the plan with trusted school staff.
Prompt ladder

1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short private question. 3 Rephrase. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time. Record actual content prompts separately from usual reading, language and communication access.
Checks and planned access
Three meanings

Wellbeing: how a person is doing daily, with support and things that matter. Mental health: part of everyone's health, including thoughts, feelings and coping or getting help; this is not the same as having a condition. Resilience: adapting after a setback, with rest, support or a changed plan; never accepting harm.
Check after the model
Ask where the invented learner adapts or uses support. Accept a defensible link in usual mode, with exact scribe/readback if needed. Use only the story.
Main hinge and decision
B: pause, adapt or ask for safe support. A wrongly requires coping alone. Check privately with a reason. If unclear, re-model and use the parallel. Pass is valid.
Parallel hinge
A: a wheel can prompt reflection and one possible step. B wrongly claims that its shape can diagnose a condition. No total, target or health judgement comes from this wheel.
Cognition and Learning
Explicit short definitions, worked example, glossary, visible model, task frames and one chosen step. Flexible grouping for a pair; reduced written load and extra processing time.
Communication and Interaction
Choice, wait time, familiar aid, pointing/drawing, exact scribe and readback. Pair discussion optional; no requirement for speech or eye contact.
SEMH

Predictable content, third-person class questions, privacy for wheel/action plan, blank/pass/fictional alternative, pre-agreed discreet step-out and supported return. No comparison or personal questioning.
Sensory/Physical
Usual accessible print/seating/communication access and quiet resets. Movement is a planning option suited to the person, never an imposed activity or physical test.
EAL
Plan in any language. Explain wellbeing, resilience and purpose with brief examples. Usual language support can convey the learner's own chosen words.
Optional private story checks
F: Which word fits asking for support? M: Which wheel areas link to the story, and why? H: Which step fits limited time or materials? Use private fictional checks only.
Misconceptions

Resilience can include rest, support and boundaries; it does not require never feeling upset or accepting harm. A small habit is not a guaranteed fix. The wheel has no diagnostic score and ordinary feelings alone do not establish a condition.
Private reflection and safe support
Wheel and one change

Support Cards page 1 is the five-sector wheel; page 2 is the private one-change plan. Sleep, Movement, People, Purpose and Downtime are prompts. There are no scores, required marks or right-shaped wheels. One realistic change per learner, not five goals. Fictional reflection, a blank or pass is equally valid. No required spending, exercise, sleep target, family contact or unsupported action.
Discreet step out

Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.
Generic help route

Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff for help to find an age-appropriate route. Seek help if a concern persists, worsens, affects everyday life or feels unsafe; you do not need a diagnosis first. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school's urgent procedure.

Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of the lesson pack, book tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school's separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. Private wheels/plans are not collected, photographed, displayed or compared for assessment. Scribing a personal card is only by agreement; the learner keeps it.
Learning evidence

Staff Evidence Sheet records explanation of the three ideas, an appropriate fictional wheel-area link, a realistic fictional step with support/barrier, learning self-check if offered, usual mode/prompts, one NS and own response. No personal wheel ratings, plan details, health/family history, names or disclosures. Private personal change remains the learner's choice; fictional evidence is equally valid. Do not infer health status, improvement or diagnosis from learning performance.
Feedback and marking

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.
Book first and scope

Use books or usual aids for fictional explanations and responses. The optional wheel/one-change card is kept by the learner and is not learning evidence to collect. This lesson claims no full statutory coverage or accreditation completion. Week 1 only; no later lesson is authored.

paragraphs: Staff answers and cover notes
These are suggested responses to the invented case, not judgements about a learner’s health. Accept other safe, reasoned answers. All personal reflection is optional and private.
Wellbeing
How a person is doing in everyday life. It includes feeling supported, having things that matter to them, and being able to manage daily life or get help.
Mental health
A part of everyone's health, linked to thoughts, feelings and coping with daily life. Everyone has mental health. This does not mean everyone has a mental health condition.
Resilience
Adapting to a setback or change, recovering in your own time, and using support when needed. It can include rest, a different plan or asking for help. It never means having to put up with harm.
Invented case key

The learner uses people by planning a safe check-in, and downtime by choosing a quiet activity. An interest could also give purpose. Asking for help and adjusting the plan can show resilience. Sleep or safe accessible movement may be discussed as possible areas, but do not infer that the fictional learner has a sleep problem or require exercise. More than one supported link is valid.
Model and one realistic change

For the invented learner: during the next agreed break, try a short quiet making activity. Ask staff what materials are already available. If materials are not available, choose a quiet drawing or reading option. Review whether the step was useful at a later agreed check-in. The making activity is the one step. Staff contact is the support to arrange it; the alternative is a fallback. A change can make a helpful habit easier to keep by agreeing when or where it fits. It must not become five separate goals.
What the wheel means

This wheel is an authored reflection aid, not a test, validated scale, diagnosis, target score or measure of how healthy a person is. The five areas are broad reflection prompts. Uneven or blank areas do not establish risk, health or failure. Do not total, compare, display or interpret pupil wheels.
Checks and tier guidance
Starter and model check

Everyone has mental health; this is not the same as everyone having a mental health condition. The invented learner shows resilience by using support and adjusting a plan. Ordinary upset can happen; do not diagnose from a feeling or classroom response.
Main hinge

A learner faces a setback. Which response can show resilience? Correct B: They can pause, adapt the plan or ask for safe support. Check privately by words, pointing or usual aid. If B or a safe equivalent with a reason, proceed. If A, unclear/no response, re-model supported adaptation and use the parallel check. Pass is not a wrong answer.
Parallel hinge
What can a wellbeing wheel tell us? Correct A: It can prompt reflection and one possible next step. The shape does not diagnose a condition.
Supported

Use the same age-respectful five-domain wheel. Offer the word bank, two example choices, a sentence frame and a completed fictional example. Pointing, drawing, usual aid or exact scribe/readback valid. Choose one realistic step with support and record content prompts.
Independent

Use the glossary, wheel prompts, visible model and usual aids. Explain the fictional example, privately choose one realistic change or fictional equivalent, and identify needed support or a barrier. Record actual independent choices and any prompts honestly.
Aspire

Keep all normal aids. Evaluate two plausible steps for the invented learner, explain the more realistic choice, and adapt it for a barrier without blaming the learner. Still choose only one step. Extra personal disclosure, more changes or longer writing are not required.
Realistic step check

The step is small enough, fits access and available resources or names needed support, and has a time/cue and fallback. No spending, sleep target, exercise or family contact is required. A barrier is context to adapt around, not personal failure. Each learner ends with one choice, even when Aspire compares two possibilities.
Self assessment

Ready to explain / With a prompt / Need another example describe learning only. All boxes start blank. Do not convert these to mood, symptom or health scores. Pass or fictional explanation can be used. Private personal goals need not be read to assess understanding.
Misconceptions
Resilience means never feeling upset or putting up with harm. Feelings can vary. Resilience can include rest, support, safe boundaries and changing a plan or situation.

A wheel score or one feeling proves a mental health condition, and a small habit guarantees a fix. Everyone has mental health. This wheel has no diagnostic score. A small step may help, while support can still be needed.
Safe delivery and evidence
Discreet supervised step out

Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.

Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of the lesson pack, book tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school's separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. Private wheels/plans are not collected, photographed, displayed or compared for assessment. Scribing a personal card is only by agreement; the learner keeps it.
Help route

Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff for help to find an age-appropriate route. Seek help if a concern persists, worsens, affects everyday life or feels unsafe; you do not need a diagnosis first. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school's urgent procedure.
Evidence and marking

Staff Evidence Sheet records explanation of the three ideas, an appropriate fictional wheel-area link, a realistic fictional step with support/barrier, learning self-check if offered, usual mode/prompts, one NS and own response. No personal wheel ratings, plan details, health/family history, names or disclosures. Private personal change remains the learner's choice; fictional evidence is equally valid. Do not infer health status, improvement or diagnosis from learning performance. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.

Current statutory secondary health-education guidance, revised in 2025 and in force from September 2026, and public-health information on universal mental health, practical wellbeing and support routes were checked for this narrow lesson.
